sara: Heads-up — after today's runtime rollout we're seeing big p99 spikes on paged-attn for long-sequence workloads. Baseline before rollout: median token 3.2ms, p99 ~14ms. After rollout: median 3.3ms, p99 ~48ms. Repro with local bench: ./bench --model redwood-13b --seq 8192 --batch 8 --kernel paged_flash_v2 --pages=on

ben: ugh. can you paste the kernel selection log + a flame/pprof? which path is chosen for these requests? :eyes:

sara: logs attached (paste below). kernel selector chooses paged_flash_v2 for seq>2048, but we see frequent fallback to slab_hybrid due to allocation failures. snippet: 
```
kernel_selector: seq=8192 -> candidate=[paged_flash_v2, fused_flash, slab_hybrid]
attempt paged_flash_v2 -> ok
alloc page table shard=23 failed -> fallback slab_hybrid
```
pprof (cpu): https://perf.redwood/pprof/1905/paged-attn-8192.html

jia: looked at the flame. allocation hot path is in kv_pager::alloc_lock and block_table shard 23 is responsible for ~42% of allocations during the run. heap summary: block_table_shard_23: 42% allocations, shard_18: 19%, rest tiny. seems like shard skew + freelist exhaustion. also mutex contention in kv_pager.

nora: that implies allocation fragmentation on block-table shards. quick mitigation options: reduce block table shard count (REDWOOD_PAGED_BLOCK_SHARDS=16) or increase kv_page_size to reduce number of pages per sequence. also try kv_cache.prefetch_window=4 to smooth access pattern. those are config-only, low-risk canary. :thinking:

mike: suggested quick canary: deploy config override on dedicated-canary-5% and run same bench: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/ri-runtime-canary REDWOOD_PAGED_BLOCK_SHARDS=16 --namespace=canary
kubectl set env deploy/ri-runtime-canary KV_CACHE_PREFETCH_WINDOW=4 --namespace=canary
./bench --target canary --model redwood-13b --seq 8192 --batch 8 --runs 20
```
Monitor p99, OOMs, and kernel fallbacks.

ben: long-term fix ideas: implement per-shard work-stealing freelist + background compaction to relocate cold pages and defragment shards. also change fallback ordering: try global hot-slab allocation before slab_hybrid fallback — that avoids the expensive fallback path that increases latency. I sketched a tiny change: 
```
// allocate: try local freelist -> try global hot-slab -> trigger background steal -> fallback hybrid
```
I'll open PR with microbench harness.

jia: also saw that kernel selection heuristics aggressively pick paged_flash_v2 for long seq but we don't account for current shard utilization in the decision. if selector consulted shard pressure (simple token-bucket per-shard) we could pick fused_flash more often when shard skew > threshold. Add a cheap metric: shard_util_pct = (allocated_pages / max_pages_per_shard). If any candidate shard_util_pct > 0.8, bias away from paged_flash.

sara: that sounds promising. plan: 1) apply config canary (nora/mike) 2) run benchmark and prod traffic canary for 24h; 3) land PR for freelist steal + background compaction; 4) follow-up PR to add shard-pressure signal to kernel selector. I'll open the tickets.

ops-bot: Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/eng-runtime/paged-attn-latency - p99 spike started at 2026-03-10T15:32:10Z, correlated with release ri-runtime-2026.03.10. Throughput graphs + OOM annotations available.

nora: small note — reducing shard count trades more metadata per shard for less skew. watch memory usage on Dedicated customers. could also attempt dynamic shard rebalance but that's more invasive.

mike: after applying REDWOOD_PAGED_BLOCK_SHARDS=16 locally I saw p99 drop from 48ms -> ~18ms in the bench run, median unchanged. no OOMs in 1h run. preliminary win but need more runs. :thumbsup:

ben: please include microbench artifacts in the PR (before/after traces, kernel logs, alloc histograms). that will help code reviewers.

sara: will do. opening ticket now and assigning. thanks all. :shipit:
